digest_gate_incident.root_cause: stale expectation in the packaged q4nm_driver.py: ad96... is the pre-re-pin value. docs/parity-id-policy.md amendment 2026-09-10 (dense BF16 decode GEMV land, receipts/2026-09-10-bf16-decode-gemv-land matrix r1-r3) re-pinned BF16 short/262 per driver: fork short f26175202f3dabe9, long 8690dc83246b39f8, 1K-ctx ff502900d2a179a5; stock short 7fc0f968789b1882, long 46108ad71157cb4d, 1K-ctx ff502900d2a179a5. Q4 pins unchanged and driver-independent (re-verified on stock in the same land matrix). Fixed in commit 328218c; gate hard-fail behavior re-proven both directions with a stub engine (mismatch -> exit 1, 18 GATE lines; match -> exit 0)
digest_gate_incident.observation_for_policy_owners: the candidate wheel predates the dense BF16 GEMV (no decode_gemv_path/subgroup-shuffle strings in its libmlx.so) yet reproduced the post-land fork pin 8690... on fork and the post-land stock pin 4610... on stock, while the land's own fork-base cell produced the pre-land ad96... on the same driver package hours earlier. The BF16 control cells are environment-coupled on this stack and have limited power as change detectors; the Q4 cells are the reliable ones.

per_dispatch.instrument: tools/q4-bw-bench (subgroup flavor), isolated kernel timing, 21 reps, M1; bit-equality 18/18 compares 0 mismatches vs the frozen ccc25c0f production shader on the four production shapes plus fasttile and oddn coverage shapes (bench-a.ndjson; --quick bench-b.ndjson agrees)

occupancy_sweep.comment: per-grid time is flat as the grid multiplies x1 -> x16 on every production shape and every side; the dispatches are not occupancy-starved and adding concurrency buys nothing
occupancy_sweep.floor: isolated measurements sit at a ~30 us dispatch/timestamp floor (min_ns 12-16 us on small shapes); oddn coverage shape shows ratio 0.61-0.67 (small-N quirk, not a production shape)

limiter: What still limits the kernel: it is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound (~1.1-1.65 GB/s against a 68 GB/s part per the candidate commit's own analysis) and not occupancy-bound (flat x1->x16 sweep). The native mapping's x-register reuse - the thing worth 0.64-0.92x on llvmpipe - buys nothing here: the M1 dispatch chain already hides the x-load traffic, and in-model context dominates (236 us/layer of Q4 GEMV in-model vs ~98 us/layer isolated sum of qkv+o+gate_up+down). The next lever for the 5.6 ms Q4 decode term is not thread mapping; it is whatever makes in-model dispatches 2.4x slower than isolated ones (cache/power state between dispatches).
